Two ways to increase SNR is to raise the signal power or decrease the noise power.

The higher the SNR, the less noise that is present.
The amount of noise in a communication system is part of the QUALITY of the system and is called the signal to noise ratio or SNR for short.
Interference is noise produced by other equipment. For example, a HAM radio operator could interfere with your TV.

What type of noise is due to thunder storms?
Thermal noise can only be reduced or eliminated by circuit design.
The random motion of the electrons results in the random generation of voltages or currents. The random voltages and currents are known as noise which distorts the information signal.
At any temperature above absolute zero, charged particles, such as electrons, exhibit random motion.
This noise is due to temperature variations in the circuit as the components heat up and cool down.
Thermal noise however, is caused by the communication systems own circuit components and design.
Environmental noise and interference from other electronic equipment can usually be eliminated or reduced by filters and limiters.
There are many types of noise that effect communication systems such as: atmospheric noise, noise from other electronic equipment (interference) and thermal noise.
Simply put, if the noise signal is greater than the information signal, the information signal is lost.
Noise is an unwanted signal in communication systems.

If a transmitted signal is not within the receivers bandwidth, the information signal is severely distorted or attenuated and the information is lost.
Although the frequency range of the human voice is from 100 Hz to 7500 Hz, it was determined that a bandwidth of 300 Hz to 3400 Hz is sufficient for commercial speech.
Notice that Band 3 is used for voice frequency. This is the bandwidth established by the FCC for telephones.
This informs engineers of bandwidth limitations for different types of communication systems.
The FCC (Federal Communication Commission) has also set guidelines and limitations to frequency bands.

How is bandwidth a limitation in a communication system?
Due to reactive component limitations it is not possible to have a system that covers a frequency range of 300 Hz to 1600 kHz.
This is why you can not receive AM radio signals on a portable telephone. The AM radio has a frequency range of 950 kHz to 1600 kHz and the telephone frequency range is from 300 Hz to 3400 Hz.
The reactance or frequency cut off points of these components limit the range of frequencies that pass through communication circuits.
The reactive components used in communication circuits determine the frequency range or bandwidth of the communication system.
Since bandwidth is a range of frequencies, the bandwidth of a system must be equal to or greater than the bandwidth of the information to be transmitted and received.
In communication systems, information is sent over transmission medium in frequencies.
Let's look at bandwidth as a limiting factor in communication systems first.
Environmental conditions such as: lightning, power lines, trees, mountains and fog can limit a communication systems effectiveness by causing noise, which in turn causes signal distortion.
Components used in communication circuits set up bandwidths to limit the frequency range of the system. This separates different types of communication systems from each other.
Communication systems are limited by the components used in their circuits and their environment.

The attraction and repulsion of the coil moves the paper cone producing sound waves.
The coil then produces a magnetic field which reacts with the permanent magnet producing attraction and repulsion.
For speaker operation, the information signal is applied to the coil.
And yes, it looks just like a dynamic microphone. In fact, dynamic devices can be used as both a microphone and speaker, a walkie-talkie is a good example.
The transducer used in output circuits for telephone systems is called a SPEAKER.
The device that changes electrical signals into voice or music signals is called an OUTPUT TRANSDUCER.
The electrical signals must be changed to voice or music signals.
On the other hand, if the output information must be in the form of voice or music signals, as in telephones and radios, a lot takes place.
Amplifiers, limiters and filters are common circuits used in output circuits for electrical signals.
If the information output is in the form of electrical signals, such as computer signals or video signals to a TV picture tube, very little takes place in the output circuits.
The output circuits set up or change the electrical signal so the information can be used.

In FM modulation (Frequency Modulation) the amplitude of the information signal changes the frequency of the carrier signal.
In AM modulation (Amplitude Modulation) the amplitude of the information signal changes the amplitude of the carrier signal.
Modulation combines two different signals, the information signal and a CARRIER SIGNAL, which will carry the information.
Modulation is a method that allows information signals to be transmitted using air as the transmission medium.

Signal processing circuits can be as simple as an amplifier for transmission through wire cables or as complex as modulators and multiplexers for transmission through the air.
The signals are conditioned by the signal processor for effective, efficient and reliable transmission.
Once the input information is in the form of electrical signals, the signal processing circuits take over.

What type of input transducer uses a magnet?
In the carbon microphone, the moving cone changes the density of carbon granules which changes the resistance of the circuit producing electrical signals.
In the piezoelectric microphone, the moving cone moves a lever that applies pressure to a crystal producing electrical signals.
In the dynamic microphone, the moving cone moves a coil in a magnetic field producing electrical signals.
In all three microphones, sound waves move a paper cone back and forth.
The transducer used in the input circuits for telephone systems is called a MICROPHONE.

TRANSDUCER - A transducer is any device that changes one type of energy into another. In radio equipment, transducers change sound vibrations to electrical signals (microphones) for transmission purposes and change electrical signals to sound (speakers) during reception.
